messages:
Riley (People Ops): Quick heads-up: effective 2026-10-01 we're adding a 5-day "compassionate care" top-up for qualifying life events and launching a small Emergency Care Stipend (one-time $750) for urgent dependent care needs while on leave. Details + eligibility below.

Maya (People Ops): The goal is to reduce stress around sudden family needs and avoid people having to choose between pay and caregiving. This top-up is integrated with existing bereavement and parental policies (not replacing them).

Ethan (Finance): Note: stipend is taxable in most locales. We'll route payments through payroll as a coded one-off so taxes are handled cleanly.

Zoe (Legal): Eligibility: employees with at least 6 months tenure. Stipend requires brief attestation (no medical docs required) to respect privacy, unless a manager requests verification for unusually large claims.

Sam (Eng): How does this interact with short-term disability or FMLA?

Riley (People Ops): It's supplemental. If someone is on paid family leave or STD, the compassionate top-up can be applied to cover gaps; Finance will coordinate to avoid double-pay. FMLA rules unchanged.

HR-bot: Policy & request form: https://intranet.redwood/workplace/policies/compassionate-care-2026. FAQ: https://intranet.redwood/people/faq/compassionate-care.

Maya (People Ops): We'll run manager training 2026-09-15 (30 min) and open an anonymous feedback channel during the pilot quarter. Pilot period = Q4 2026.

Ethan (Finance): Payroll action items: implement stipend code, sample run on 2026-10-05.

Sam (Eng): Appreciate the privacy-first approach.

Riley (People Ops): Thanks all 64F please DM if you have edge cases; post major questions here so we can update the FAQ.
